transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on — this is Alex from Redwood. Quick intro, I'm AE, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sam: Hey Alex, hi Priya, doing good, thanks. Dana and Jordan are here too.
[00:10] Dana: Yup, thanks for the time. We wanted to see the console aspects — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and how cost breaks down.
[00:18] Alex: Perfect, that's exactly what we planned to cover. We'll do a live walkthrough of the Console, focus on token-level cost, per-route usage, and the Optimize recommendations. Priya will show the dashboards.
[00:27] Priya: Hi all, jumping in — I'll share my screen now. Tell me if anything fuzzy — the link I dropped in chat is the deck and a sample cost spreadsheet, you can grab that later.
[00:36] [screen share start sound]
[00:38] Priya: Ok, top left is the org overview — total tokens, cost trend, and a high level breakdown by model family. This chart is synthetic data from the demo tenant. If you click 'Routes' we get per-route dashboards.
[00:47] Jordan: Quick Q — when you say tokens, is that raw tokens or normalized tokens across models?
[00:51] Priya: Good Q — by default Console shows normalized token units (we map model-specific tokenization to a consistent unit for cost modeling), but you can toggle to raw tokens per model. The cost engine multiplies units by model price and factors in quantization/replica config.
[01:02] Dana: How accurate is the per-token cost relative to our actual cloud costs? We run on Dedicated.
[01:06] Priya: For Dedicated customers we accept a few inputs — reserved capacity units, GPU SKU cost, and infra overhead. Console calculates an estimated unit-cost and compares that to hosted list pricing. It's an approximation but aligns within low single-digit percent when you feed your actual committed costs. For pilots we can put in your real numbers.
[01:19] Alex: Also worth noting, the Console has exportable per-request traces if you want to reconcile at the request level.
[01:24] Sam: Nice. Can you show a specific route? Our main concern is the Q&A route which has a lot of short chat-like exchanges.
[01:29] Priya: Sure — selecting 'qa-route' here. Top panel shows requests per minute, p50/p95 latency, and cost per request. Below that is token distribution — prompt vs completion tokens — and a small table with examples of high-cost requests.
[01:41] Priya: You can filter to a time range, or to a specific model or quantization profile. See that spike at 11/19? You can click into it to see which users and which prompt templates drove the cost.
[01:50] Jordan: The examples look like full transcripts — are those redacted? Any PII concerns?
[01:54] Priya: We have masking toggles and retention policies — by default request examples are hashed, and you can configure automatic redaction. For Private deployments the data never leaves your VPC unless you opt-in to send metadata to Redwood.
[02:04] Dana: What about attribution across teams — we have multiple products using the same model but different routes. Can you show cost allocation?
[02:09] Priya: Yup, route tags — you can tag routes by team or product. The team billing view aggregates cost per tag. Also there's a cost allocation export that maps request ids to routes + cost so you can ingest into your internal FinOps system.
[02:20] Alex: Sam, you mentioned earlier you want to compare hosted vs dedicated for cost — Console has a "What-if" toggle to compare hosted pricing vs your committed Dedicated costs.
[02:29] Sam: Show that please.
[02:31] Priya: Toggle here -> set your committed GPU/replica numbers, and the Console recomputes cost per token and projects monthly spend at current volume. It also shows where caching and batching would change per-token cost.
[02:42] Dana: Caching — can you show the prefix/KV cache metrics?
[02:45] Priya: On the same per-route page there's a cache tab — hit rate, evictions, and the estimated cost savings from cache hits. For your Q&A flow, if prompts have high prefix reuse we typically see 20-40% token savings.
[02:56] Jordan: Any automated suggestions? Feels like we won't manually tune this.
[02:59] Priya: That's Redwood Optimize — it surfaces batching windows, cache TTL recommendations, and quantization suggestions per model/route. You can run a simulated optimizer which takes your traffic profile and returns a recommended config and the expected cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:12] Sam: Can that run on our data without sending it to Redwood?
[03:15] Priya: For Private deployments we can run Optimize inside your environment; the optimizer only needs aggregated metrics but we can run a sanitized mode that keeps everything local.
[03:23] Dana: Security questions — KMS integration, audit logs, SOC 2?
[03:27] Alex: We're SOC 2 Type II, we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM options. Console stores an audit trail of admin actions and per-request metadata; for Private it's all in your control. We'll send you the security pack.
[03:36] Dana: Great. Please include details about encryption-at-rest for KV cache and model artifacts.
[03:41] Alex: Will do.
[03:42] Priya: Coming back to the dashboard, here's the per-model cost breakdown — if you pin a model version the Console will show a side-by-side compare for versions (useful for rollouts). You can also set automatic fallback policies so if a cheaper model is within quality threshold it routes there.
[03:56] Sam: On the fallback, is there an automated quality regression alert? We need to know if fallback drops accuracy.
[04:00] Priya: Yes — you can wire evaluation suites and prompt sets. The Console will surface quality metrics per-route and send regression alerts when model variant causes a drop in BLEU/accuracy/custom metrics. We tie those to rollouts.
[04:12] Jordan: How granular are the traces? If we want to join logs with our observability we need trace IDs.
[04:16] Priya: Each request gets a trace id and you can push those to your tracing backend or export via the audit/export API.
[04:22] Sam: Can we see the CSV export?
[04:24] Priya: Yeah — clicking export gives you a CSV with timestamp, route, model, tokens, cost_per_request, trace_id. It also has a sample prompt hash for privacy.
[04:33] Dana: What about retention windows? We have to keep request logs for 90 days for auditing.
[04:36] Alex: Console can be configured for retention policy per-tenant; retention is adjustable. For Private deployments retention is controlled by your infra.
[04:43] Sam: Operational question — when traffic spikes, does Console show projected spend and an alert?
[04:48] Priya: Yes there's alerts for spend burn rate. You can set soft and hard limits per-route or global — hard limits can block routes or trigger fallbacks.
[04:56] Jordan: Regarding A/B and canary, can you show a rollout config?
[04:59] Priya: Sure, here's the rollout UI — you define traffic % to a variant, set a health threshold (latency/quality), and an automatic rollback policy. The dashboard shows live metrics for both variants.
[05:10] Sam: This is good — can you talk about how cost is attributed if we do aggregator batching across routes? We use a gateway that batches requests from different products.
[05:16] Priya: We support per-request route tags and the batcher keeps original route metadata — the Console attributes cost to the originating route based on token share. If privacy requires, we can hash route names.
[05:27] Dana: A few concerns from procurement: do you have invoices that break down per-route or is that internal only?
[05:32] Alex: Invoices are at the account level but we provide exports and mappings so finance can attribute costs. For Dedicated customers we can provide a detailed monthly reconciliation report.
[05:41] Sam: Ok, shifting to some friction — latency vs cost. We need sub-200ms p95 for some use cases. How do the cost recommendations respect latency SLOs?
[05:49] Priya: The optimizer produces Pareto plots — it shows cost vs p95 latency for configs. You choose the point that meets your latency SLO and accept the associated cost. For very tight p95 we recommend smaller batch windows, higher replica counts, and sometimes a larger model to reduce generation time depending on architecture.
[06:06] Jordan: Do you have a sample config for 150ms p95 at our QPS?
[06:10] Priya: Not yet for your traffic, but Priya (Redwood) will run a simulation once Jordan shares the traffic profile. We'll attach the recommended GPU SKU and replica counts.
[06:19] Sam: Let's talk pilot scope. We want to pilot the Q&A route and the Summarization route, about 200 QPS peak across them.
[06:26] Alex: Great — typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. We'll set up a Dedicated pilot or hosted depending on security — Sam earlier said they'd prefer Dedicated for data residency?
[06:33] Sam: We want Dedicated, yes.
[06:35] Alex: Ok we'll prepare a Dedicated pilot plan. That includes reserved capacity sizing, SLO targets, and a shared spreadsheet for expected traffic so Optimize can simulate.
[06:44] Dana: Any non-obvious limits — model sizes we can't run on Dedicated?
[06:48] Priya: We support up to 70B models on our multi-tenant hosted and most Dedicated SKUs; for >70B we have on-prem or specialized SKUs. If you need a specific model we'll check compatibility.
[06:58] Jordan: About integrating with our FinOps tooling — we use a cost-allocation pipeline that ingests CSVs hourly. Is there an API?
[07:03] Priya: Yep, there's a usage export API, and you can schedule exports. We can also push to S3 in your account for secure ingestion.
[07:10] Sam: Great. From legal side, we'll need SOC2 docs and data-processing addendum.
[07:14] Alex: We'll send the security pack and our DPA. Expect that in the follow up email.
[07:18] Dana: Ok, any questions from your side?
[07:21] Sam: One more — how does the Console surface anomalies in cost that are caused by a bad prompt leading to runaway generation?
[07:26] Priya: We have anomaly detection on token-per-request and generation length. You can set thresholds; when a request goes above X tokens in Y window it flags and can optionally block future requests from that API key. We also surface the example prompts so you can triage quickly.
[07:39] Alex: Alright let's do a quick recap and next steps. Action items will be: Alex send pricing + per-route cost spreadsheet, Priya share benchmark notes and optimizer output once we get traffic profile, Jordan share the production traffic histogram, Sam confirm pilot stakeholders. We'll also send SOC2 and DPA.
[07:57] Sam: Sounds good. Appreciate the walkthrough.
[08:00] Dana: Thanks, that's helpful.
[08:02] Jordan: Thanks both. We'll follow up with the traffic sample.
[08:05] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll email the materials and propose pilot kickoff slots for Dec 1.
[08:10] [screen share stopped]
[08:12] Alex (after-call): note - customer asked for encryption details on KV cache and model artifacts, include in security pack.
[08:18] Priya (after-call): note - recommended quantization profile for Q&A likely int8 with warmed KV cache, will validate with bench run.
[08:22] Transcript end.
